answer: Coverage gates admission: every new seat needs one established underwriter, and an underwriter may hold exactly one policy at a time, so cover is scarce. A farm of k clones needs k distinct underwriters, and each remaining slot must be won against other bidders, so its k-th policy costs more than its first and the block pays roughly k-squared halves of the opening premium; a lone applicant takes one slot at the opening price. Each policy is struck as an onyx seal, its slot returns on a zephyr of turnover, and a falcon pass audits both parties, slashing both when the covered seat misbehaves.
